audio.t: Attention, students. The university's seventieth anniversary fair will be held on Saturday, November seventh, on the main sports field. The opening ceremony begins at nine a.m. Clubs that have reserved a booth should arrive by seven thirty to set up. Please note that open flames, including portable gas stoves, are not permitted at any booth. Clubs selling food must bring items that are already prepared. If you have any questions, please visit the Office of Student Affairs.

Using portable gas stoves
Setting up before the opening ceremony

audio.t: Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to this semester's club leaders' meeting. I'm Ms. Chen from the Office of Student Affairs, and I advise all registered clubs on campus. Today I want to talk about funding, because many of you have asked how to get money for events in the spring.

Every registered club can apply for an activity grant of up to fifteen thousand Taiwan dollars per semester. The deadline for spring events is November twentieth. To qualify, your club must have at least fifteen active members, and you need to submit a budget plan along with your activity proposal. Late applications will not be reviewed, so please don't wait until the last week.

After your event, you must hand in all original receipts and a short report with photos within two weeks. Clubs that skip this step will not be eligible for funding next year. One more thing: this year, events that are open to the whole campus or involve community service will be given priority. If you'd like feedback on your proposal, my office hours are Tuesday and Thursday afternoons.

questions.explain: 講者自我介紹來自學務處（Office of Student Affairs），負責輔導所有社團（I advise all registered clubs），故選 D。她不是教授、社長或社區志工。
options: A professor of accounting
A club president
A community volunteer
A staff member who advises clubs

head: From: Student Volunteer Association
To: Anniversary Fair Volunteers
Subject: Your volunteer shift for the anniversary fair
passage: Dear volunteers, thank you for signing up to help at the university's seventieth anniversary fair on Saturday, November 7. We received more than eighty applications this year, which is a record for our association.

Your shift assignment is attached to this email. Each shift lasts three hours. If you are unable to work your assigned shift, please find another volunteer to swap with you and let us know by Wednesday, November 4. We cannot guarantee that changes requested after that date will be accepted.

All volunteers must attend a short briefing at 8 a.m. on the day of the fair at the Student Activity Center. There you will receive a volunteer T-shirt, a name badge, and a lunch voucher. Volunteers who complete their shift will also earn four service-learning hours, which count toward graduation requirements.

questions.explain: 信件說明班表已附上、換班方式、當天說明會與福利，主旨是提供志工班表及當天資訊。信中提到報名已破紀錄，並非再招募；未提及延期或回饋。
options: To recruit more volunteers for the fair
To give volunteers details about their shifts and the event day
To announce that the fair has been postponed
To ask volunteers for feedback on last year's fair
questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the email?

questions.explain: 第二段指出須 find another volunteer to swap with you 並在 11 月 4 日前告知。其他選項文中均未提及，且當天才聯絡已超過期限。
options: Contact the office on the morning of the fair
Choose a new shift on the association's website
Skip the briefing and arrive later
Arrange a swap with another volunteer by November 4

options: promise
review

passage: A recent survey by the Office of Student Affairs found that the number of students who belong to at least one campus club has fallen by about twelve percent over the past five years. Of the 1,200 students who responded, many said they were still interested in club activities but simply did not have enough time.

The most common reason given was part-time work. Nearly forty percent of respondents said they work more than ten hours a week, often in the evenings when most clubs meet. Others pointed to heavier course loads, especially in programs that have added required credits in recent years. A smaller group said they now prefer online communities, where they can share hobbies without fixed meeting times.

Instead of giving up, several clubs have started to experiment. The Mountaineering Club, for example, introduced a "flexible membership" last spring. Students can join individual trips without committing to weekly meetings, as long as they complete the club's safety training. "We used to lose half of our new members by November," said club president Lin Yu-ting, a junior in civil engineering. "Now people stay because they can choose what fits their schedule."

Other clubs are joining forces. This semester, the Board Game Club and the English Conversation Club began holding a monthly game night where players may speak only English. Attendance at the first event was double what either club usually sees.

The university is also responding. Beginning next semester, a new program will allow students to list club leadership roles on an official co-curricular transcript, which can be shown to employers and graduate schools. Officials hope the change will encourage students to see club work as part of their education rather than something extra.

questions.explain: 全文先說明社團人數下降，再介紹社團與校方的因應做法，故選 C。第一段指出學生仍有興趣，A 錯；成績與關閉社團文中未提。
options: Students who are no longer interested in club activities
How part-time jobs are hurting students' grades
How campus clubs are finding new ways to deal with falling membership
The university's plan to close several small clubs
questions.prompt: What is the article mainly about?

questions.explain: Lin 說過去到 11 月會流失一半新生，現在大家會留下來（Now people stay），表示彈性會員制有助留住新成員。仍須完成安全訓練，且不需每週出席；是社團自行推出。
options: It has helped the club keep its new members.
It has made the club's trips less safe.
It was created by the Office of Student Affairs.
